<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/9036):

>## Summary
>- Creates `TESTING.md` as the single source of truth for unit test conventions (naming, function naming, placement, additional rules)
>- Updates `DEVELOPMENT.md` Code Conventions to link `TESTING.md` instead of the `.claude/skills/code-formatting` skill
>- Updates `AGENTS.md` key references table to point to `TESTING.md`
>- Removes `.claude/skills/code-formatting/` — conventions now live in `TESTING.md` where both humans and agents can reliably discover them
>- Updates `.claude/SKILLS.md` to remove the code-formatting entry
>
>## Why
>The jira-agent's review phase was not enforcing HyperShift's `When [condition], it should [behavior]` test naming convention because the convention lived only in a Claude skill that agents don't reliably auto-load. Moving conventions to a standard markdown file at the repo root makes them discoverable via `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `AGENTS.md` references.
>
>See also: companion PR in openshift-eng/ai-helpers that strengthens the solve and review commands to check these files.
>
>## Test plan
>- [ ] Verify `TESTING.md` contains all conventions previously in `.claude/skills/code-formatting/SKILL.md`
>- [ ] Verify `DEVELOPMENT.md` Code Conventions section links to `TESTING.md`
>- [ ] Verify `AGENTS.md` key references table updated
>- [ ] Verify `.claude/skills/code-formatting/` is removed
>- [ ] Verify `.claude/SKILLS.md` no longer references code-formatting
>
>🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
